content:
As I have probably mentioned more than once, I have been working on Tex2Lean and two of my recent projects were to formalize OpenAI's FPRAS algorithms in a manner where there is a high level description of the algorithms and proof of correctness of those algorithms.

Naturally, I wanted to see if I can use some parts of the lean proof from OpenAI, and surprisingly, my extension struggled to make usage of anything. Of course, part of the issue is that OpenAI went on to prove existence of Turing Machine but one expects that there has to be high level components that are re-usable as after all, I was trying to formalize those FPRAS based on OpenAI's preprints.

I would be interested to hear your thoughts on how you are going about reusing existing formalizations in your projects as while "end-to-end formalization" is great but this also feels like reinventing everything [except things on mathlib] from scratch.

Best,
Kuldeep
Are you interested in only correctness or do you need time/space complexity?

Anyway, the broader answer is to build human-written robust libraries of algorithms like I am trying to do in Algolean for algorithmic theory (we are not super concerned with implementations on the theory side), or more broadly CSLib. Depending on what kind of algorithms you wish to formalize, it might make sense to build out your own library or contribute to CSLib.
Some research labs tend to maintain their own libraries and repositories.

I am interested in both correctness and time/space complexity.

On a side note, Since CSLib didn't have way to formalize time and space complexity when I began working on Tex2Lean, I began a parallel effort in trying to model.

I had chat with @Alexandre Rademaker recently and I have been studying your proposals, and I see lot of overlap in my efforts and yours; there is one usage of pure that I am struggling with as well; here is the DSL that Tex2Lean formalizes into: https://github.com/meelgroup/arlib/blob/main/docs/dev/Program-Language.md.; this documentation is, unfortunately, LLM generated and mostly for LLM agents to read; I have been planning to write a proper one for a while]

In that case you might be interested in our library Algolean github.com/Shreyas4991/Algolean. It’s a framework we developed to encode the numerous models we see in algorithmic theory and provide a way to abstract literature algorithms away.

( I am guessing you might be discussing my related CSLib PRs if you spoke to Alexandre. Algolean substantially extends it).
